subtitle: Archaeology, Archaeogenetics, Epigraphy & Paleoclimate of the Harappan Civilization

events.title: Monumental Kot Diji City Wall at Mohenjo-Daro
events.summary: Redating of the 7-meter-thick mudbrick wall as an Early Harappan city fortification of the Kot Diji phase. Refutes Wheeler's interpretation as a post-Harappan flood embankment and demonstrates monumental urbanism already in the 4th millennium BCE.

events.title: Peak of Mature Harappan Urbanism
events.summary: Standardization of brick proportions (1:2:4), orthogonal grid-plan cities, monumental drainage systems, great baths, and granaries across all major centers of the Indus Basin.

events.title: Canonization of the Indus Script & Dholavira Signboard
events.summary: Corpus of over 400 standardized signs on steatite seals, copper tablets, and the monumental signboard at the north gate of Dholavira. Modern NLP entropy models demonstrate rigid syntax and linguistic encoding.

events.title: Long-Distance Trade with Mesopotamia (Meluhha Contacts)
events.site: Ur, Kish, Tell Asmar, Persian Gulf
events.summary: Royal inscriptions of Akkad (Sargon) mention ships from Meluhha. Indus stamp seals, etched carnelian beads, and lapis lazuli in Mesopotamian royal tombs attest direct maritime trade via Dilmun and Magan.

events.title: Tidal Dockyard & Semi-Precious Stone Workshops at Lothal
events.summary: Large baked-brick basin (approx. 214 x 36 m) with sluice gate connected to the Gulf of Khambhat. Specialized workshops producing micro-drilled stone and carnelian beads; continuous use into the post-urban phase.

events.title: Genome Sequencing Rakhigarhi I6113 (Autochthonous Two-Stream Model)
events.summary: Complete absence of Steppe ancestry (Steppe_MLBA) and Anatolian farmer admixture in the Mature Harappan period. Profile derives from approx. 65% Iranian Neolithic-related lineage and approx. 35% autochthonous South Asian hunter-gatherer ancestry (AASI).

events.title: 4.2k Event & 113-Year Megadrought (Dharamjali Speleothems)
events.summary: High-resolution oxygen (d18O) and carbon isotope curves document four abrupt, multi-decadal monsoon failures culminating in a 113-year megadrought (c. 1580–1470 BCE). Primary driver of de-urbanization.

events.title: Orderly De-Urbanization & Eastward Settlement Shift
events.summary: Abandonment of planned metropolises and monumental drainage infrastructure. Shift from winter-rain wheat/barley to summer-monsoon millets and rice; transformation into small-scale rural village communities.

events.title: Late Pleistocene Paleo-Sutlej Avulsion (Ropar Surface)
events.summary: OSL datings demonstrate that the tectonically driven avulsion of the Paleo-Sutlej away from the Ghaggar-Hakra system already occurred in the Late Pleistocene. Harappan settlements along the drainage thus relied primarily on summer monsoon rainfall.
sources: Singh, Tandon et al. (Comm. Earth Env. 2026)

events.title: Pre-Early Harappan Ceramic Presence in Gujarat & Ganeshwar AMS Dates
events.summary: New AMS 14C series and stratigraphic syntheses in South Asian Ceramics trace early Indus ceramic networks in Gujarat back to c. 3700–2900 BCE and anchor the Ganeshwar ceramic horizon.

events.title: East Asian Agrarian Wave Along the Southern Himalayan Foothills
events.summary: Whole-genome analysis of 115 individuals from northern Pakistan identifies two East Asian dispersal waves along the southern Himalayan foothills, beginning with an agrarian rice-farming wave around 4,800 BP.

events.title: Multi-Isotope Study of Husbandry and Herd Mobility at Dholavira
events.summary: Combined carbon (δ13C), oxygen (δ18O), and strontium (87Sr/86Sr) tooth enamel data from cattle (Bos) and water buffalo (Bubalus) distinguish C3/C4 foddering strategies and attest local and regional herd mobility in the Kutch basin.
